newsitem.title: USA: American Pad sees improved performance.
newsitem.headline: American Pad sees improved performance.

text.p: American Pad & Paper Co said on Monday it expects to improve its financial performance later this year, helped by accretive acquisitions.
The company reported first-quarter net income of $0.16 per share, up from $0.15 the year before and just above the First Call consensus estimate for the first quarter of 1997, also $0.15 per share.
The company's shares were trading up 1-1/8 to 17-3/8 early Monday.
American Pad said that, while satisfied with its first quarter performance, it plans to do better later this year.

"We believe the factors impacting sales this quarter are short-term and we expect sales to return to market expectations in the second half of the year," company Chairman/Chief Executive Charles Hanson said in a statement.
The Shade-Allied acquisition is to be completed in July, the company said, and its acquisition pipeline "is full."
"We will continue to drive growth through accretive acquisitions and are evaluating opportunities in both new product lines and add-ons to our existing lines," Hanson said.

Factors affecting first-quarter results included a substantial reduction in planned flow to office-supply superstores due to the impact of consolidation activities and to a more conservative inventory strategy by our customers due to a perceived softening in the uncoated free sheet area, the company said.
American Pad & Paper makes paper-based office products.
